binaryprimitives-endianness-protocols.title: Make binary protocol endianness explicit with BinaryPrimitives
binaryprimitives-endianness-protocols.short: Do not leave integer byte order implicit
binaryprimitives-endianness-protocols.summary: BinaryPrimitives reads and writes numeric values with an explicit byte order directly over spans, fitting network and file formats.
binaryprimitives-endianness-protocols.why: Implicit byte order makes protocol code harder to audit and can break interoperability when a format requires a specific ordering.
binaryprimitives-endianness-protocols.tips: Follow the external format specification and test round trips against known byte sequences including boundary values.

sslstream-certificate-validation.title: Treat SslStream certificate validation as a TLS trust boundary
sslstream-certificate-validation.short: Secure transport requires authenticating the peer as well as encrypting bytes
sslstream-certificate-validation.summary: SslStream can establish TLS, but security also depends on correct host-name, chain, and certificate validation behavior.
sslstream-certificate-validation.why: A callback that accepts every certificate removes meaningful peer authentication even though traffic remains encrypted.
sslstream-certificate-validation.tips: Prefer platform validation and make any custom rejection rules explicit, including tests for certificate renewal.

readerwriterlockslim-read-heavy-state.title: Use ReaderWriterLockSlim selectively for read-heavy shared state
readerwriterlockslim-read-heavy-state.short: Balance concurrent readers against added synchronization complexity
readerwriterlockslim-read-heavy-state.summary: ReaderWriterLockSlim allows multiple readers while excluding writers, but its state transitions are more complex than a simple lock.
readerwriterlockslim-read-heavy-state.why: It can help with sufficiently long and frequent reads, while short critical sections may gain nothing after overhead and contention.
readerwriterlockslim-read-heavy-state.tips: Start with simpler synchronization and consider it when measurements show reader contention is a material bottleneck.

concurrent-collection-count-hot-path.title: Do not use concurrent collection Count as permission for the next operation
concurrent-collection-count-hot-path.short: Prefer one atomic-style try operation over check-then-act code
concurrent-collection-count-hot-path.summary: Another thread can change a concurrent collection after Count is observed, so the value cannot guarantee a following dequeue or removal.
concurrent-collection-count-hot-path.why: Check-then-act code creates races and can add unnecessary global-state work on hot paths.
concurrent-collection-count-hot-path.tips: Use operations such as TryDequeue that directly report success, and treat Count primarily as observational data.

dbdatareader-streaming-results.title: Stream large query results with DbDataReader
dbdatareader-streaming-results.short: Process rows incrementally instead of materializing every result
dbdatareader-streaming-results.summary: DbDataReader provides forward result consumption suitable for processing large result sets without first building an in-memory collection.
dbdatareader-streaming-results.why: Materializing every row increases memory with result size and delays useful work until loading has progressed.
dbdatareader-streaming-results.tips: Keep connection, command, and reader ownership clear and propagate cancellation through asynchronous reads.

activity-tags-baggage-boundaries.title: Separate Activity tags from propagated baggage
activity-tags-baggage-boundaries.short: Distinguish span attributes from context intentionally carried downstream
activity-tags-baggage-boundaries.summary: Activity tags primarily describe the current span, while baggage is intended to flow with distributed context to downstream work.
activity-tags-baggage-boundaries.why: Propagating high-cardinality or sensitive values indiscriminately increases telemetry cost and information exposure.
activity-tags-baggage-boundaries.tips: Put only necessary context in baggage and define a policy that excludes secrets and personal data from telemetry.

aspnet-antiforgery-browser-state.title: Protect browser-authenticated state changes from request forgery in ASP.NET Core
aspnet-antiforgery-browser-state.short: Account for credentials that browsers attach automatically
aspnet-antiforgery-browser-state.summary: Applications using browser-managed authentication state must consider whether a state-changing request can be induced from another origin.
aspnet-antiforgery-browser-state.why: Being authenticated does not by itself prove that the user intended a particular state-changing request.
aspnet-antiforgery-browser-state.tips: Apply ASP.NET Core antiforgery protections where the authentication and UI model require them, rather than relying only on SameSite behavior.

processstartinfo-argumentlist.title: Pass process arguments separately with ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList
processstartinfo-argumentlist.short: Avoid hand-building one quoted command-line string
processstartinfo-argumentlist.summary: ArgumentList represents each process argument separately, reducing manual quoting mistakes for values containing spaces or quotes.
processstartinfo-argumentlist.why: String concatenation can accidentally change argument boundaries and is especially risky when values originate outside the program.
processstartinfo-argumentlist.tips: Avoid invoking a shell when it is unnecessary, and keep the executable path trusted or strictly validated as well.

unity-closure-allocation-hot-loop.title: Avoid unnecessary closure allocation on Unity hot paths
unity-closure-allocation-hot-loop.short: Measure delegate and capture allocation in per-frame code
unity-closure-allocation-hot-loop.summary: A lambda that captures surrounding state may require a closure object, which can accumulate GC pressure when created frequently.
unity-closure-allocation-hot-loop.why: Per-frame creation turns individually small allocations into a steady stream of garbage and possible collection pauses.
unity-closure-allocation-hot-loop.tips: Confirm allocations in the Profiler first, then prefer immediate work or reusable callbacks where that remains clear.

x509certificate2-private-key-lifetime.title: Manage X509Certificate2 and private-key object lifetimes explicitly
x509certificate2-private-key-lifetime.short: Dispose certificate and key wrappers according to ownership
x509certificate2-private-key-lifetime.summary: X509Certificate2 and private-key objects returned from APIs such as GetRSAPrivateKey can be tied to native or operating-system resources.
x509certificate2-private-key-lifetime.why: Unclear ownership in long-running services can retain key handles and complicate certificate rotation.
x509certificate2-private-key-lifetime.tips: Never log private key material, define certificate ownership, and dispose returned disposable key objects appropriately.
